title: Compliance Readiness Radar & Evidence Automation Playbook
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Summary: Create a reproducible, cross-functional playbook and milestone radar that consolidates SOC2/ISO readiness checkpoints, SSO/SAML signoff, and audit-log evidence collection. The playbook prioritizes automation of evidence capture from Redwood Console and Dedicated deployments to reduce manual evidence collection by 75% and shorten audit cycles.

Goals: (1) Define milestone radar with owners and exit criteria for SOC2/ISO readiness; (2) Instrument Console + Dedicated deploys to produce verifiable evidence artifacts (logs, config snapshots, access lists) into a retention store; (3) Implement lightweight automation to collect, package, and sign evidence for auditors; (4) Provide an executive dashboard for assurance status by customer cohort.

Milestones & Target Dates: 
- M1 (Feb 12): Milestone radar drafted and socialized with Security & Eng leads.
- M2 (Feb 26): Evidence taxonomy finalized (log types, retention windows, manifest format).
- M3 (Mar 12): Proof-of-concept evidence collector (Console export + S3 package) validated in staging.
- M4 (Mar 30): SSO/SAML integration checklist and test matrix completed; two enterprise customers validated.
- M5 (Apr 08): Audit package automation (signed bundles + manifest) deployed to staging for internal audit.
- M6 (Apr 15): Playbook published, executive assurance dashboard live, and runbook handed to trust team for audits.

Acceptance criteria: 
- A machine-readable manifest format exists and is documented (Confluence link in comments).
- Evidence collector can produce reproducible bundles for Console and Dedicated environments and attach a signed digest.
- Owners for each radar milestone identified, with clear start/stop gates.
- Automated tests that verify artifact generation in CI for key evidence paths.

Out of scope: Full end-to-end SOC2 audit engagement (this ticket prepares packaged evidence and readiness signals, not the external audit execution).

Risks & Trade-offs: 
- Trade-off between automation scope and schedule: prioritizing a minimal signed bundle format (faster) vs. complete built-in archival (slower). We plan minimal viable evidence bundles for April and iterate.
- Data-sensitivity: evidence bundles may contain metadata that requires redaction. Security asks for a KMS-backed signing process; this adds 2-3 sprint work in ENG.

Notes for Eng: ENG tickets listed under dependencies own the collectors and storage integration. Engage with ENG-5320 early (KV cache logs retention) to avoid last-minute schema changes.
